name: command-bar-wears-the-space-tint
description: The command bar reads its accent from the space tint that C++ pushes into its document (PushOverlayTheme), and draws a bound action's shortcut as one keycap per key. Both are read from the live /commandbar document rather than from a screenshot, because the tint is a computed property and the caps are a count. The fixture's startup space carries tint oceanBlue, which rust/atrium-core/src/tint.rs resolves to #0F2B46, so the expected triplet is 15 43 70.

actions.note: AC: the push landed in this document, not only in the sidebar's

actions.expression: (() => { const c = getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.cbcard')).backgroundColor; const cs = c.match(/^color\(srgb\s+([\d.]+)\s+([\d.]+)\s+([\d.]+)/); const rgb = cs ? cs.slice(1, 4).map((v) => Number(v) * 255) : (c.match(/[\d.]+/g) || []).map(Number); const want = [247, 236, 237]; return String(rgb.length >= 3 && want.every((v, i) => Math.abs(v - rgb[i]) <= 4)); })()
actions.note: AC: overlayAccent defaults to brand, so the card mixes the fixed crimson (color-mix(--ov-accent 6%, #FBF7F8) with --ov-accent pinned to rgb(176 58 72)), not the oceanBlue tint. color-mix() results serialize as color(srgb 0..1) rather than rgb(0..255) in this Chromium build, so the probe scales that form before comparing - a rendered colour, not only the variable on the document
AC: fontFamily reports the declared name even when the file failed to load, so check the font actually loaded

assertions.desc: the command bar document carries the startup space's tint (oceanBlue #0F2B46)
the card's rendered background-color reflects the brand accent (overlayAccent's default), not the neutral plate - the fix for the vacuous-assertion pattern
the caps read in macOS order, so a sibling scenario's reading still holds
fontFamily reports the declared name even when the file failed to load, so check the font actually loaded
